adapter.goal: Map Material Switch state, semantics, chrome, and motion facts into the shared component parity packet so interaction-heavy Material foundation work can be queued by evidence.
source_precedence: Material spec and Material Web for visual intent, switch icons, token vocabulary, and transition timing
Compose Material3 for toolkit switch semantics, touch target sizing, state model, and interaction source behavior
Material UI for web-facing Switch defaults and input semantics
Base UI only as a headless a11y fallback if switch semantics need a second opinion

limitations: This first Switch packet proves the harness can represent an interaction-heavy Material control; it is not a complete visual parity claim.
The current packet relies on Fret bundle semantics/interaction facts and existing timeline screenshot scripts; pixel-level motion deltas against upstream Material Web are future hardening.
Motion/chrome checks intentionally stay in ecosystem/fret-ui-material3 unless a later packet proves a true mechanism defect.

facts: A Material Switch is a toggle control with checked state and disabled state.
Activation toggles the boolean state only when enabled.
Keyboard and pointer activation should produce the same selected-state outcome.
Fret Material3 Switch sets SemanticsRole::Switch and checked state from the bound model.
Switch::test_id stamps the pressable semantics while centered_fill_with_chrome_test_id derives '<base>.chrome'.
The gallery exposes enabled, overridden, disabled, icons-both, and selected-icon-only variants with stable ids.

checks.expected: A fresh Material Switch bundle should prove switch role, checked state, disabled state, activation, and stable root/chrome ids for default and icon variants.

promotion.reason: Switch semantics and activation are interaction outcomes that need bundle-backed proof.

parts.label: Material 3 Switch touch target and chrome surface

facts: Material Switch keeps the visual track/handle token-driven while the interactive target satisfies minimum touch-target sizing.
Track, handle, and state layer sizes are Material component tokens.
The visual chrome should remain centered inside the larger interactive box.
Switch uses enforce_minimum_interactive_size for the pressable target.
Switch resolves track, state layer, handle, pressed-handle, and with-icon handle sizes from Material switch tokens.
centered_fill_with_chrome_test_id keeps the token-driven visual chrome centered and automation-addressable.

checks.expected: Switch should separate minimum interactive target sizing from token-driven visual chrome and expose the chrome id.

promotion.reason: The touch-target/chrome split is recipe-owned but foundation-backed and should be preserved before refactors.

parts.label: Material 3 Switch state layer, ripple, and focus chrome

facts: Switch hover and press drive state-layer/ripple behavior.
Focus-visible is expressed through focus ring and component chrome rather than generic core policy.
Material Web uses different focus selectors for track, handle, and icon chroming.
Switch uses material_ink_layer_for_pressable_with_ripple_bounds with thumb-relative ripple bounds.
Switch separates pressed/hover/focus-visible state-layer and chrome interactions before resolving Material tokens.
Existing focus-visible and state-matrix scripts cover pointer focus, keyboard focus-visible, hover, pressed, disabled, and icon variants.

checks.expected: Switch state-layer, ripple, and focus chrome should have focused diagnostics before foundation refactors.

promotion.reason: State-layer/focus behavior is interaction-sensitive and should be hardened with focused scripts before shared foundation edits.

parts.label: Material 3 Switch handle and icon motion

facts: Material Web switch uses an overshoot easing for handle-container position.
Switch icon opacity, transform, and color transitions use short independent durations.
Reduced/disabled motion collapses animation while preserving final checked-state output.
Switch encodes Material Web handle overshoot easing and icon opacity/transform/color durations in the recipe.
Switch keeps icon nodes alive across toggle frames so transitions remain visible.
Timeline screenshot scripts capture handle overshoot, icon motion, icon color crossfade, and chrome crossfade.

checks.expected: Switch motion-sensitive behavior should have fixed-timestep-capable scripts before recipe or motion foundation cleanup.

promotion.reason: Motion parity must stay script-backed; screenshot timelines should later gain structured sidecar predicates or pixel checks.

facts: Material Web exposes an icons mode with both selected and unselected icons.
Material Web also exposes show-only-selected-icon behavior.
Disabled switches preserve semantic disabled state while rendering disabled chrome.
Switch::icons(true) renders both on/off icon layers.
Switch::show_only_selected_icon(true) hides the unselected icon and rotates the selected icon in.
The gallery exposes both icon modes plus disabled variants.

checks.expected: Switch icon modes should be exposed in the gallery with stable selectors and diagnostics before icon-motion refactors.

promotion.reason: Icon-mode coverage should become a component fixture when structured paint/scene predicates are available.
